content.body:
The Bf-110 was fast and heavily armed, its original design was intended to be a heavy escort fighter. While a sound idea, the 110 was sadly outclassed by single seat fighters during 1940 and was in need of fighter escort itself in many cases. None the less its tightly grouped and heavy nose gun package was second to none in any fighter the day.
With good wing loading, the 110 enjoyed a tight turning radius for its size. However, it was under-powered and in a dogfight it was unable to hold its own as any fight it was in grew more intense, speeds would fall with each successive turn around the circle. It could manage hit and run attacks very well however.
When the Bf-110 hits something, that thing dies. If you can bring the guns onto target they will knock down anything. Stay fast and use teamwork and surprise to be effective in this piggy. If you find yourself switching to the tail gunner to defend yourself, you are all but cooked. With the tight turning circle an aggressive pilot can bring the nose around on an attack and use shock as effectively as guns. No Allied pilot ever wants to see the nose of the 110 pointing at them, and if you can make them believe they might get that view some will panic. All you need is an enemy in your sights for two seconds and its all over but for the burning and the screaming.
Bf 110's were often referred to as "Zerstörers" ("Destroyers").
CREW POSITIONS: 1 Pilot 2 Tail Gunner
